topics.title: The neem tree and its uses

learn.hook: Why would anyone brush their teeth with a twig? Meet the neem tree — India's bitter but brilliant friend!
points: 'Neem Baba' is a lesson about the neem tree and the many ways it helps people.
The neem tree (scientific name Azadirachta indica) is native to the Indian subcontinent and grows well in hot, dry places.
Its leaves taste bitter. Traditionally, neem twigs (called 'datun') have been used to clean teeth.
People traditionally keep dried neem leaves with stored grains and woollen clothes to keep insects away. Oil from neem seeds is used in some soaps and natural insect repellents.
A big neem tree gives cool shade, and its small white flowers smell sweet.

example.q: Read: Outside our school stands a huge neem tree. Its bitter leaves rustle in the breeze, and its thick branches give cool shade in May. Grandpa still cleans his teeth with a neem twig. Every year Ma puts dried neem leaves in the rice tin to keep insects away. The children call the tree 'Neem Baba' because it seems wise, old and kind. Give two uses of the neem tree from the passage.
steps: Grandpa cleans his teeth with a neem twig → use 1.
Ma keeps dried neem leaves in the rice tin to keep insects away → use 2.
Its branches give cool shade → use 3.
example.answer: Any two: cleaning teeth with a twig, keeping insects away from rice, giving cool shade.

learn.reallife: You may see neem trees along roads and in school compounds, and neem in soaps and toothpastes on shop shelves.

Neem is famous for its bitter taste.

It grows well in hot, dry places.

quiz.q: In the passage, why do the children call the tree 'Neem Baba'?
options: Because it was planted last week
Because it seems wise, old and kind
quiz.explain: The last line gives the reason: it seems wise, old and kind.
quiz.mistake: Does not read the reason given in the passage

quiz.q: In the passage, how does Grandpa use the neem tree?
options: He cleans his teeth with a neem twig
He makes tea from its bark
quiz.explain: The passage says Grandpa cleans his teeth with a neem twig.
quiz.mistake: Confuses Grandpa's use with Ma's use

quiz.q: Why does Ma put dried neem leaves in the rice tin?
quiz.explain: The passage says she does it to keep insects away.
quiz.mistake: Guesses instead of finding the reason in the text

quiz.q: What does neem taste like?
quiz.explain: Neem leaves are well known for their bitter taste.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up neem with fruits like mango or tamarind

quiz.q: A neem twig used to clean teeth is traditionally called a:
quiz.explain: 'Datun' is the name for a twig used as a natural toothbrush.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the traditional word

quiz.q: In the passage, "its thick branches give cool shade in May." Why is shade useful in May?
options: May is very hot in most of India
Trees have no leaves in May
quiz.explain: May is one of the hottest months in most of India, so cool shade is welcome.
quiz.mistake: Does not use general knowledge about Indian weather

quiz.q: Where does the neem tree naturally come from?
quiz.explain: Neem is native to the Indian subcontinent.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the tree is native to India

quiz.q: In the passage, the leaves "rustle in the breeze". 'Rustle' means to make:
quiz.explain: Leaves moving in the wind make a soft, light rustling sound.
quiz.mistake: Does not use the context of leaves and breeze

teach.ask: Gappu perches on a branch: 'This neem tree is my home. But what does it do for humans?'
teach.praise: Tweet! Neem gives shade, keeps insects away and even cleans teeth. My home is a superhero!
teach.nudge: Can you tell me one way people use neem leaves or twigs?

learn.hook: One tree can give shade to a whole playground for a hundred years. What can one child give back?
points: Conservation means protecting and carefully using nature — trees, water, animals and soil — so that it lasts for the future.
We can help by planting trees, saving water, not wasting paper and following the 3 Rs: Reduce, Reuse, Recycle.
Van Mahotsav, a tree-planting festival, is celebrated in India in the first week of July. World Environment Day is on 5 June.
In the Chipko movement of the 1970s, villagers in the Himalayan hills hugged trees to stop them from being cut down. ('Chipko' means 'to stick' or 'hug'.)
Compound words join two words to make one: rain + water = rainwater; sun + light = sunlight; wild + life = wildlife.

example.q: Think it through: Sort these actions into Reduce, Reuse or Recycle: carrying a cloth bag instead of taking a new plastic one; using an old jam jar as a pencil holder; sending old newspapers to be made into new paper.
steps: Not taking a new plastic bag means using less → Reduce.
Using the jar again for a new job → Reuse.
Turning old paper into new paper → Recycle.
example.answer: Cloth bag → Reduce; jam jar pencil holder → Reuse; newspapers to make new paper → Recycle.

learn.reallife: Turning off the tap while brushing, carrying a steel water bottle and planting a sapling on your birthday are everyday conservation.

games.title: Reduce, Reuse or Recycle?
items: turning off the tap while brushing
carrying a cloth bag
using an old bottle as a plant pot
giving old clothes to a younger cousin
sending newspapers to be made into new paper
melting old glass bottles to make new ones

quiz.q: What does 'conservation' mean?
options: Protecting nature and using it carefully so it lasts
quiz.explain: Conservation is about protecting and wisely using natural things.
quiz.mistake: Confuses 'conservation' with 'conversation'

quiz.q: Which tree-planting festival is celebrated in India in the first week of July?
quiz.explain: Van Mahotsav ('festival of forests') is celebrated in the first week of July.
quiz.mistake: Mixes it up with other festivals or national days

quiz.q: On which date is World Environment Day observed?
quiz.explain: World Environment Day is observed every year on 5 June.
quiz.mistake: Confuses it with other important dates

quiz.q: In the Chipko movement, what did villagers do to save trees?
quiz.explain: 'Chipko' means to stick or hug; villagers hugged trees to stop them being cut.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the meaning of 'Chipko'

quiz.q: Which is an example of 'Reuse'?
options: Using an old jar as a pencil holder
quiz.explain: Using something again for a new purpose is reusing.
quiz.mistake: Confuses reuse with recycle or waste

quiz.q: Which is a compound word?
quiz.explain: 'Sunlight' is made of two words: sun + light.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any word with a suffix is a compound word

quiz.q: Which action saves water?
options: Turning off the tap while brushing your teeth
Washing the car every day with a hose
Playing with the garden pipe for hours
quiz.explain: Turning off the tap stops water from being wasted.
quiz.mistake: Does not see which action wastes water

quiz.q: What is the opposite of 'protect'?
quiz.explain: To protect is to keep safe; to harm is to hurt. Guard, save and shield are synonyms.
quiz.mistake: Picks a synonym instead of the opposite

teach.ask: Gappu worries: 'People keep cutting trees. What does conservation mean and how can children help?'
teach.praise: Tweet tweet! Conservation means protecting nature: plant trees, save water and reduce, reuse, recycle. Thank you!
teach.nudge: What are some things a child can do to protect nature?

learn.hook: Where is the bird? In the tree, on the branch, among the leaves — prepositions are word maps!
points: A preposition shows the relation of a noun or pronoun to another word — often place, time or direction.
Place: in (inside), on (touching the surface), under (below), beside (next to), between (two things), among (more than two).
Time: at for exact times (at 7 o'clock), on for days and dates (on Monday, on 5 June), in for months, years and seasons (in July, in 2024, in summer).
Use 'since' for a starting point (since 2015) and 'for' for a length of time (for ten years).
Direction: into, out of, across, through, towards ('The squirrel ran up the trunk').

example.q: Think it through: Fill in: 'The children sat ___ the shade of the neem tree ___ 4 o'clock ___ Sunday.'
steps: 'Shade' is an area we are inside → in.
A day of the week → on.

learn.reallife: Giving directions — 'The shop is beside the temple, across the road' — uses prepositions all the time.

items.text: The parrot is sitting ___ the branch.
Divide the laddoos ___ the two brothers.
Share the sweets ___ all the children in class.
Grandpa has lived in this house ___ 1990.

quiz.q: Fill in: 'The cat is hiding ___ the bed.'
quiz.explain: Hiding happens below the bed, so 'under' fits.
quiz.mistake: Picks a preposition of time instead of place

quiz.q: Fill in: 'The school opens ___ 8 o'clock.'
quiz.explain: We use 'at' for an exact clock time.
quiz.mistake: Uses 'in' or 'on' for clock times

quiz.q: Fill in: 'My birthday is ___ 10 March.'
quiz.explain: We use 'on' for dates and days.
quiz.mistake: Uses 'in' because March is a month, ignoring the date

quiz.q: Which sentence uses between or among correctly?
options: Ravi sat between Asha and Meena.
Ravi sat among Asha and Meena.
Ravi sat between the five children.
Ravi sat on between Asha and Meena.
quiz.explain: 'Between' is used for two people or things; 'among' for more than two.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up between and among

quiz.q: Fill in: 'We have waited ___ two hours.'
quiz.explain: 'For' is used with a length of time like two hours.
quiz.mistake: Uses 'since' with a length of time

quiz.q: Fill in: 'The monkey jumped ___ the pond with a splash.'
quiz.explain: 'Into' shows movement from outside to inside.
quiz.mistake: Does not choose a direction preposition for movement

quiz.q: Which word is a preposition in: 'The squirrel ran up the neem tree'?
quiz.explain: 'Up' shows the direction of running in relation to the tree.
quiz.mistake: Confuses the preposition with the verb or noun

quiz.q: Fill in: 'Mangoes are sweetest ___ summer.'
quiz.explain: We use 'in' for seasons.
quiz.mistake: Uses 'on' for seasons

teach.ask: Gappu is lost: 'My friend says the seeds are on, in or under something. How do these little words work?'
teach.praise: Chirp! Prepositions tell where and when. My seeds are in the bowl, on the table, under the neem tree!
teach.nudge: Do prepositions tell us only about place, or also about time?
